[spoiler=What if everything went PERFECT for Srpka?]
[b][i]WHAT IF EVERYTHING WENT PERFECT FOR SRPKA?[/i][/b]

[i]Inspired by Possible History on YouTube. I recommend checking his videos out.[/i]

Good morning class. This dispatch is a little different than the others. I have decided to create an alternate history for my nation as an experiment to see how alt-history stories and dispatches can work within Erene. For this one specifically, it will be going over what Srpka and East Shamat as a whole would look like if history went ideally for Srpka. Enjoy!

[hr]
[hr]

Srpka today as a nation has its highs and lows. It is one of the most resource rich nations on the planet, yet at the same time has a developing economy that is falling behind its neighbors. It has a large population and several trade and industrial hubs, yet is very isolated or gets straight up ignored by the international community due to its proximity to Hydronia and Karcovshkie, two relatively powerful nations that have much more influence and spotlight. Srpka had suffered the curse of an imperialist, colonial neighbor for centuries, and suffered the consequences of it up to the modern day. Today, we will answer the question; what if everything went perfect for Srpka?
[hr]
[b]SRPKAN INVASION OF HYDRONIA, 1728[/b]

Now, to begin our journey, I felt it was best to start our journey in 1728 for a number of reasons. One, going further back in time and changing things around in Srpkas favor can ensue Butterfly Effects across the timeline, making it harder to get a refined look at this scenario. Two, the Srpkan invasion of Hydronia is where we can shift things the most in Srpkas favor. Three, I dont want to risk making the dispatch too long, else I risk making mistakes over the time it takes to create this.

Anyways, to start off with, can we let Srpka just march on Hydropolis? No. Absolutely not. The Holy Hydronic Empire, even with its own shortcomings, is simply too big of a pill to swallow. It had more than twice the population of Srpka, it retained a large colonial empire and its frozen climate near the North Pole brought brutal winters that made an extended war difficult. While Srpka had an impressive army for its size, it was not enough to compare to one of the largest empires in history. Srpka simply couldnt play against those odds and gain a total victory.

So, what do we do? Simple. We need to un-stupid the Srpkan battle plan. The original battle plan was to try and shock the people within Turvekistan and the other mainland provinces by Hydronic incompetence, attempting to start a rebellion to support the invasion. The Srpkans need to realize that the Holy Hydronic Empire was not on its way to collapsing like they thought it was. Additional forces need to be prepared because the Hydronics arent going to falter within a matter of months.

With Sakara in the war, the Srpkans have an ally and a weak Hydronic army to fight due to an expanded frontline. If Sakara and Srpka dont get greedy and keep their lines stable, then eventually, negotiations could commence. The peace treaty wouldnt be too harsh on the Empire, however Srpka would definitely take Bugostan while Sakara would annex territories in Turvekistan. Some extreme Srpkan nationalists might claim that they would also annex Aekarxa if they won, however I dont believe the Hydronic Empire would accept the loss of such a defendable position over a war they could continue if they wanted. Either way, the record is set clear - the Hydronics have been bested, and they are no longer absolute on the continent.
[hr]
[b]ISLAMIC REVOLUTION IN SRPKA, 1792
KARCOVS REVOLUTION, 1798[/b]

This might not be surprising, but it is very hard to change the mindset of people hundreds of years ago. We simply cannot take out the religious persecution and racism from Srpka. However, we could shorten the failed revolution and prevent the destruction caused by it. Lets say the Islamic revolutionaries fail to connect their territories, or one of their commanders is killed in battle, or the Srpkan government manages to prevent a revolt to the scale of our timeline.

There are many ways to shorten the war, but no matter what way, we have to shorten it by 2 years. If the revolution ends in 1798 instead of 1800, the Srpkans have time to witness Karcovshkies birth via Karcovs Revolution. Here, the Khanate has three options. One, dont interfere in the Revolution and the timeline is mostly unchanged. Two, fund whichever side can benefit Srpka the most from an economic standpoint. Three, outright launch an invasion of Kurvokia and both make an enemy out of them and gain defensive territories out of it. For the sake of making things interesting, we have them choose option three.

With a Srpkan invasion from the west, Karcovs Revolution is suddenly facing a major third faction that is much more powerful than either rebel or Kurvokian armies. Remember, this Srpka is the one with an alliance with Sakara, a more accomplished military and a more stable populace than the one of our own timeline. I have no doubt in my mind that the Srpkan armies, assuming the Kurvokian and rebel forces dont suddenly get over their differences, could overrun Kurvokia within a few years.

If we assume a Srpkan victory here, then Id imagine very little Kurvokian territory would be lost to Srpka, simply because the invasion already took place on the outskirts of the Khanate, across the Eastern Ridge. The monarch would keep his place, however a more liberal and democratic constitution would be put in place. The constitution put in place is essentially a compromise between the rebels and Kurvokia. Srpka has now completely prevented the rise of Karcovshkie as we know it, as the government of Karcovshkie is almost completely opposite to the Karcovshkan government of our timeline.

[hr]
[b]MODERN ERA[/b]

After the alternate Karcovs Revolution, there isnt much to be done with Srpka, as we have already set them on a path to success. We could tweak minor things, like sending Srpkan supplies to the Bobian Revolt or going into economic and political specifics, but thats boring and I wanted to focus on expansion of power.

Anyways, since Srpka already owns Bugostan, there is no Bugo-Tarzanite War in the 1960s. This could, funnily enough, mean that the continent of East Shamat in this timeline is more stable than our own. Now, since we have started our journey at 1728, there are many butterfly effects that can affect the timeline in unpredictable ways, so I cannot predict the specifics of what the economies, militaries or diplomacy of this large nation look like, especially considering Sakara probably still exists as an independent nation here. Instead, I will end this historical discussion at the THEP-EDU War of our own timeline but with Greater Srpka, an independent Sakara and a liberal Kurvokia replacing Karcovshkie thrown into the fray.

[b][i]If Srpka joins the THEPs side[/i][/b]

Assuming the THEP is unchanged, if Srpka joined Hydronias side in the conflict, not much would actually change. If Srpka joins THEPs side in the conflict, then Sakara and Kurvokia would either remain neutral or follow Srpkas lead.

In the peace talks of our timeline, Srpka was disproportionately underrepresented in the talks considering they were an active participant for THEPs side, and trying to protect East Shamat from Elseyran influence. In this timeline, Srpka would hopefully have a larger and stronger say on the matter, although I dont imagine the peace deal itself would change much.

Yes Im still pissed off about being ignored in the peace deal, how could you tell?

[b][i]If Srpka joins EDUs side[/i][/b]

If Srpka joined the EDUs side, then Hydronia would have it pretty hard in this timeline. The Hydronians would be in a rough spot, perhaps being forced to concede more to the Hochdeutsche. The Sakarans are kind of a wild card in this scenario. Either they join Hydronias side and Srpkan lines are seriously strained or they join Srpkas side and make Hydronias life even more miserable. Kurvokia is the same story, although they have a higher chance of staying neutral considering they arent on the front lines of a global conflict.

[hr]
[b]STATISTICS[/b]

Srpkas position is seriously improved in this timeline thanks to its military victories and some lucky timing of the events around them. The Srpka of our timeline has about a trillion dollar economy. The Srpka of this one could have up to one and a half trillion, depending on their global influence and influence on their neighbors.

I cant predict which alliances Greater Srpka joins or its diplomacy with the nations around it, so guessing alliances is very difficult. I can imagine that the Khanate is still in power and even more wildly popular than in our own timeline thanks to decent and responsible leadership and governance of the state.

Our Srpka has around 60 million people within its borders, a fair amount considering its size and climate. The Srpka weve created, with its stronger economy and its other benefits, could have around 75 million people within its borders, maybe even 80 depending on if territory is taken from Kurvokia in 1800.

I have detailed several examples of the same point; this Greater Srpka has the power to take on just about any challenge that rears its ugly head.

[hr]
[hr]

[b]CONCLUSION[/b]

If you took the time to read through this, I really appreciate it, this took a lot of scrolling through other nations factbooks and trying to make sense of history and the issues of alternate history scenarios. I had a lot going on while writing this but I really enjoyed thinking about it and coming up with a story for it. Sya[/spoiler]
